02 / SERVICE DESIGN CASE STUDY

A journey should
work for everyone.

A speculative design exploration into how transport planning can become calmer, clearer and more inclusive.

Service designUX research planningInteraction designAccessibility
“The best route isn't always the fastest one.”
THE CHALLENGE

Transport information is often optimized for schedules, not people.

Journey tools can make travelers compare unfamiliar route codes, transfers and accessibility details all at once. MATKA explores a more supportive decision flow where people can choose based on confidence, clarity and individual needs—not just minutes.

FRAMING THE EXPERIENCE

Three design principles

◎

Clarity first

Make the next action unmistakable. Prioritize destination, time and transfers over system terminology.

♧

Access by default

Surface step-free boarding as part of planning—not as an afterthought or hidden filter.

↝

Confidence in motion

Explain why a route is recommended and what happens at each stage of a journey.

PROPOSED SERVICE JOURNEY

From intention to arrival

DISCOVER“I need to get there.”

Start with places, not line numbers.

DECIDE“Which journey suits me?”

Compare clarity, transfers and access.

TRAVEL“I know what comes next.”

Keep one meaningful step in focus.

ARRIVE“That felt manageable.”

Complete the journey confidently.

RESEARCH & VALIDATION PLAN

What we would test next

01. Task-based usability test

Can a first-time visitor plan a route in under two minutes without assistance?

02. Accessibility walkthrough

Can people identify step-free choices using keyboard and screen reader navigation?

03. Decision confidence interview

Do recommendation explanations make the chosen route feel trustworthy?

Concept transparency

This is a portfolio prototype. The problem framing and research plan are design hypotheses; they are not presented as findings from completed user studies. Route data is illustrative.
